title: Neypes v. Court of Appeals
summary: The Supreme Court introduced the 'fresh period rule' in appeals, holding that a party who files a motion for reconsideration has a fresh 15-day period from receipt of the denial to file a notice of appeal. This standardized the period regardless of whether a motion for reconsideration was filed.
doctrine: A party litigant may file a notice of appeal within 15 days from receipt of the order denying the motion for reconsideration (fresh period rule). This fresh period applies regardless of the period already consumed before the filing of the motion for reconsideration.
fullText:
CORONA, J.:

The issue is the proper computation of the period within which to file a notice of appeal when a motion for reconsideration has been previously filed.

The Court standardizes the appeal period in this manner: a party litigant may either file his notice of appeal within 15 days from receipt of the Regional Trial Court's decision, or file it within 15 days from receipt of the order denying his motion for reconsideration.

The fresh period rule gives the party the full 15-day period from receipt of the denial of the motion for reconsideration within which to file the notice of appeal. This is consistent with the principle that rules of procedure should be liberally construed to promote their objective of securing a just, speedy and inexpensive disposition of every action.
